_note: A REAL rubric from a shipped campaign, kept as a worked example. It is the exact
logic that used to be hardcoded in grade_pe_fit.py.
Read it to see the level of specificity a rubric needs. Note that the
disqualifier reasons explain the business logic ('secondaries buyers buy LP
interests, not companies') rather than just saying 'not a fit' — that is what
makes a graded list reviewable by someone who wasn't there when it was built.
Do not reuse this for a different offer. Copy TEMPLATE.json instead.
name: lmm-pe-deal-origination
campaign: Selling off-market owner origination to lower-middle-market PE firms and family offices doing control buyouts

grades.A: Dedicated BD / origination / deal-sourcing role at a qualifying firm. They own the problem and have budget language for it.
grades.B: Investment decision-maker (Partner / MD / Principal / Founder / CEO) at a qualifying firm with no dedicated BD desk — they source personally.
grades.C: Investment professional at a qualifying firm, but junior, or the firm already has a BD lead who is the better entry point.
grades.D: Wrong person at a right firm: operating partner, CFO/compliance, or an exec of a portfolio company rather than the investing firm.
grades.E: Wrong firm: not doing control/LMM buyouts (asset manager, VC, secondaries, single-sector fund), or the row has no ICP evidence.
